reflection: The notebook shows that volume-based ideas (QQQ volume surge and the Apple-minus-QQQ volume surge) are the only ones with a sign of life, helping in 2023 and 2025 but missing in 2022 and 2024. Almost every price-based variant (signed, scaled, relative, smoothed) either duplicated an existing factor (similarity above 0.7) or failed in 2024. Volume that is one-day noisy seems to be the weak point. Next I will test smoothed and longer-baseline volume measures to reduce day-to-day noise, and pair volume with a direction or trend sign so it is not blind to whether the market rose or fell. I will also try a drawdown-from-high measure and NVDA volume, which have not been tested yet.

lessons.name: qqq_signed_volume_surge
lessons.lesson: Multiplying QQQ's volume surge by the sign of its daily move gave a near-zero, unstable signal (helped only Logistic Regression, missed in 2024), so the direction tag added noise rather than a consistent edge.

lessons.name: aapl_gap_scaled_by_range
lessons.lesson: Dividing the overnight gap by Apple's daily range made it a weak variant of the gap idea, which was already regime-dependent and too unstable across years.

lessons.name: aapl_5d_return_vol_scaled
lessons.lesson: Scaling the 5-day return by 20-day volatility produced a near-copy (0.98) of AAPL_mean_return_5d, so it had no new information and failed in 2022 and 2024.

lessons.name: qqq_close_location_1d
lessons.lesson: QQQ's close position within its daily range is very similar to QQQ_return_1d (0.75) and flipped sign across years, so it carried no stable new information.

lessons.name: aapl_volume_surge_minus_qqq_surge
lessons.lesson: The relative volume surge helped in 2023 and 2025 but missed in 2022 and 2024, likely because the one-day 20-day baseline is noisy and ignores the market's direction, so it is only a weak promising signal.

lessons.name: nvda_volatility_10d
lessons.lesson: NVDA's 10-day volatility helped only in 2023 and was dominated by the 2024 miss, so the peer-volatility level did not carry a consistent next-day signal for Apple.

factors.name: qqq_volume_ratio_smooth5d
factors.hypothesis: qqq_volume_to_ma20 missed in 2022 and 2024 probably because a single-day volume spike is noisy; averaging the volume ratio over 5 days should keep the sustained participation signal and drop one-day noise.

factors.name: aapl_volume_surge_vs_60d_minus_qqq
factors.hypothesis: The 20-day baseline is noisy and reacts to recent spikes, which may explain the 2022 and 2024 misses; a 60-day baseline measures Apple's relative volume against a steadier norm.

factors.name: aapl_drawdown_from_20d_high
factors.hypothesis: Distance from the 20-day closing high captures how far Apple has pulled back, which is not the same as the moving-average gap or cumulative returns already in the set and may show short-term mean reversion.

factors.name: nvda_volume_surge
factors.hypothesis: Heavy volume in NVDA, the highest-volatility AI peer, may signal sector positioning that leads Apple's next move; this volume channel has not been tested for a peer.

factors.name: aapl_signed_volume_surge
factors.hypothesis: Pairing the market-wide QQQ volume surge with Apple's own volume surge signed by Apple's up or down day gives Apple-specific direction information that the market volume factor lacks.

factors.name: qqq_trend_60d
factors.hypothesis: The relative volume surge ignores the market regime; a 60-day QQQ trend indicates whether heavy relative volume happens in an uptrend or a downtrend, which may explain its 2022 and 2024 misses.
